doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Opening greetings and the warm Town Hall reception
summary: Monk Rowe opens the filming; they talk about their reception at Town Hall the night before, Joe Williams' absence, George Wein, and their fiftieth anniversary.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: We are filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive today, in New York City. And I am very pleased to have two of America’s treasured musicians, Jackie Cain and Roy Kral.
Good afternoon. I think it’s safe to say you’re treasured musicians, because I saw the audience reaction last night at Town Hall.

Yeah. You know it was kind of funny because standing backstage when they said that Joe [Williams] wasn’t going to appear, because he was ill, and everybody went awww, and I thought oh gee, now we have to jump into his shoes. But then when we came out we got such a wonderful reception.

It was such a warm reception. And I talked to George Wein who was backstage, and I said, “George, it was so wonderful. We walked out, we hadn’t done anything, and yet we got this great reception.” He says, “well, we’ll have to do more of this.” So that was very nice.
You remind him of that occasionally.
I think quality always wins out. And I’ll give you a belated congratulations on your fiftieth anniversary together as a couple, both in music and in marriage.
Well we’ve been married 48 years. But we’ve been working together for 50. © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-
